$comment: Gate-clause wiring register. Seeded 2026-08-25 from the E0..E11 exit-gate audit.
wired   = a production path reaches the named symbol; the checker verifies it and fails on 0.
unwired = honestly dormant; reason must say what would have to change. Reported on green runs.
Claiming wired when nothing calls it is the defect this register exists to make impossible.

A CLAUSE IS THE UNIT OF CLAIM, AND HALF A CONJUNCTIVE CLAUSE MAY NOT BE ENROLLED. 2026-09-09: E0-de06-artifact-denial-audit was added here as `wired` for DE-06's audit clause and REMOVED the same day. The clause reads 'object put/get AND rejected-key attempts are audited'; only the rejected-key conjunct was wired, and a successful download grant still writes nothing. The symbol genuinely had callers, so the checker was green and correct -- what was false was the CLAUSE-LEVEL claim the key asserts. Enrolment here reads as delivery; a partly-delivered clause belongs in its finding until the whole clause holds. See docs/replatform/epics/E0-foundation/findings.md, E0-F010.

providerCapabilityClaims (optional) = the provider-capability values this clause's reason asserts, checked against the source that declares them. Added 2026-09-06 (W4U1) after E5-2's reason described artifactExportMode for weeks after PR #353 changed it, because nothing read the sentence.

E9-1-service-reconciler.reason: E9's exit gate opens with `desired state` and `placement`; SVC-002 is the control-plane half. TIMING: SVC-002-design.md 9.2 predicted this clause would land `unwired`, on the GO-BOOK's 2026-08-28 ruling that an E9 clause was PREMATURE `no real service-execution symbol to track until SVC-002 lands ... so a clause would be vacuous`. That ruling named its own release condition and it is now met: SVC-002 lands the symbol AND its arming path in one commit. PRODUCTION CALLERS: 0 at base (the symbol did not exist), 2 at head as the guard's own `countProductionCallers` measures it -- and those two lines are ONE composition site in server/src/index.ts, the dynamic-import binding plus the call, inside the `config.distributedExecutionEnabled && distributedExecutionDatabases` block. The measured figure is stated rather than the intuitive one because the guard counts the `const { createServiceReconciler } = await import(...)` line too (its import-stripping regex only blanks static `import ... from` forms). That block builds the reconciler, drives it on a `nextDelayMs` backoff timer, and stops it on SIGTERM/SIGINT. Registered inside that block for MIG-002's measured reason, not by copying it: flag-off allocates no `aoa_app` pool, so `runInTenant` would have nothing to open and unconditional registration would be a throw rather than a safety net. WHAT THE CLAUSE CLAIMS, NARROWLY: when a `services` row exists with `desired_state='running'` and a `service_generations` definition for its generation, the reconciler creates EXACTLY ONE `service_instances` row and EXACTLY ONE `service` job for it, in one transaction, and never a second -- idempotently across ticks, across concurrent passes, and across a writer that takes no lock at all. WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM, and each of these is the difference between this clause and the epic's gate: (1) NOTHING CREATES A SERVICE. `services` has one insert in the tree with ZERO production callers and SVC-002 adds no route (SVC-007 owns create/update/pause/resume/stop), so on a real deployment the tick reads an empty window and converges nothing -- E9's exit gate is NOT met by this ticket and this ticket does not claim it is. (2) `service_generations` likewise has ZERO writers, so even a hand-inserted service stalls at `{action:'none', reason:'no_generation'}` rather than starting with an invented command; the unreadable-intent branch is a deliberate stall, not a default. (3) It converges zero instances to one and then goes quiescent: `recordServiceHealth` is the only writer of `service_instances.status` and has no consumer, so nothing here drives an instance terminal (SVC-003). (4) `drain` means a draining target is not SELECTED for a new instance; moving or stopping an instance already running on a draining target is SVC-003/SVC-005. (5) A submitted service job is placed `queued`/`no_eligible_target` unless a daemon advertises `workload.service` with a free service slot, and E9-F002 stays open. PROVEN, NOT DECLARED: server/src/__tests__/service-reconciler.integration.test.ts (17 cases: SCHEMA, T1a-T1d, T2, T3a/T3b x3/T3c, T4, T5, T6, T7 + a NAMED positive control) plus packages/db/src/__tests__/service-instance-live-predicate.test.ts (4 cases). TWELVE mutants were applied to the shipped source, VERIFIED APPLIED in the rebuilt dist before their result was believed, run, and reverted; each killed at least one case while the named positive control (`T4 POSITIVE CONTROL`, pure `decideJobPlacement`) stayed green under every one: drop the partial unique index (2 red), widen its terminal predicate with 'pending' (2 red), widen the loser's catch to a bare `catch {}` (1 red, T1d), revert `reconciliationId` to `randomUUID()` (1 red, T1c), catch the 429 INSIDE the transaction (1 red -- T2's zero-INSTANCES half, with its zero-JOBS half still green, i.e. exactly the orphan wedge), delete the reconciler's sweep filter (1 red, T3a, on the reason and the no-error assertion rather than on a vacuous zero-instances one), delete the `desiredState` admission predicate (3 red -- and this is the one GENUINE base-tree red: before SVC-002 `serviceSourceIsAdmitted` had no such predicate), change it to `ne('stopped')` (2 red: `paused` and `deleted`, with `stopped` still green, which is the allow-list-vs-deny-list discrimination), and -- added in the review pass -- anchor the per-organization service sweep at the head instead of its cursor (1 red, T5: `expected [ ...(2) ] to deeply equal [ ...(5) ]`, two of five services converged and the other three starved forever, which was a REAL BUG in the first revision of this diff and is fixed), drop the `notExists` convergence predicate from `listReconcilableServices` (2 red, T4 + T6: a converged service never leaves the sweep window, so the window never shrinks and a restarted process re-walks finished work forever), and wrap the sweep cursor on a SHORT page without checking it was fully processed (1 red, T7: with three STALLED services -- and today every service stalls at `no_generation`, because `service_generations` has no writer -- a budget-truncated page restarts at the head every tick and the tail behind them is never reached), and revert the live-instance predicate from inlined SQL literals to drizzle's `notInArray` (2 red: the compiled statement carries three BIND PARAMETERS, and a parameterised `status NOT IN ($1,$2,$3)` cannot be proven to imply the LITERAL predicate of `service_instances_live_service_uq`, so once postgres-js's prepared statement is promoted to a generic plan the partial index is dropped and the sweep sequentially scans `service_instances` -- reproduced on PostgreSQL 18 in review). ★ TWO MUTANTS THE DESIGN NAMED DID **NOT** KILL, AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN DROPPED: (i) changing the observed-state predicate from non-terminal to `status='healthy'` leaves the suite GREEN (measured 14/14, before the review pass added T5), because that predicate and the index predicate are THE SAME CONDITION at two layers -- it reds only together with dropping the index, and then T4's `created` is [1,1,1]; (ii) removing the advisory lock leaves the suite GREEN, and so does removing the `FOR UPDATE` -- the serialization case reds only when BOTH go, so it pins the pair and neither member is individually necessary. Both corrections are written into the test file beside the cases they concern. THE AUTHORITY IS THE INDEX, NOT THE LOOP: `service_instances_live_service_uq` (migration 0275) binds every writer including ones not yet written, and T1a exercises it with two LOCK-FREE inserters on separate connections rather than through the reconciler.

E9-2-service-supervisor.reason: E9's exit gate names supervision of a service instance; SVC-008b is the daemon half (SVC-008-design.md §11.2). WIRED, and enrolled as `wired` rather than the `unwired` the design predicted, because the design wrote that line when the constant widening was still hypothetical: SVC-008b actually dispatches to the symbol. PRODUCTION CALLERS: ONE, as the guard measures it — the `handoff.offer.job.workloadType === "service"` branch in `runLifecycle` (packages/worker-daemon/src/supervisor/supervisor.ts), which sits on the shipped lease path `createSupervisor` -> `accept` -> `runLifecycle`, and `createSupervisor` is composed in production by `lifecycle/dispatch-runtime.ts`. WHAT THE CLAUSE CLAIMS, NARROWLY: a service job reaches a worker and is SUPERVISED AS A SERVICE — launched via `startProcess` (an acknowledgement, not a completion), health-ticked from `processStatus`, stopped through a cancel->kill ladder whose verdict comes from an observation, and terminalized with the frozen service-instance events. It does NOT claim services are MANAGED: health semantics + the `service_health` -> `recordServiceHealth` projection are SVC-003's, restart/checkpoint are SVC-004's, drain/generation are SVC-005's, and there is still no human path to create a service (SVC-007). SVC-008b adds NO consumer of `recordServiceHealth` and no `service_health` state projection: the symbol's reference set is UNCHANGED by this diff, base to head, as the register's own counter reports. (The reason line previously said `recordServiceHealth` "keeps its zero production callers"; that number was wrong — the counter reports the same non-zero figure at base and at head. The substance, no new consumer, is what the clause needs and is what is asserted here.) PROVEN, NOT DECLARED: packages/worker-daemon/src/__tests__/svc-008b-service-supervisor.test.ts (T1-T7 + a NAMED positive control) was observed 12-red / 2-green against the unchanged tree, and six mutants were killed — deleting the dispatch (12 red), synthesizing `healthy` on an unwitnessed read, deriving the stop verdict from `ProcessSignalResult.accepted` instead of its observation, dropping the per-tick fence check, dropping the capability-freshness stop, and killing before the graceful rung. The positive control stayed green under every one. server/src/__tests__/u0-d1-placement-reachability.test.ts carries T0: the committed worker-b ceiling now leaves the shipped daemon's DERIVED hello offerable a real service job through the real `evaluateStaticLeaseEligibility`; reverting the constant reds T0 and the exact-equality pin while both batch cases stay green. RESIDUAL, ON THE RECORD: a service run is bounded at RUN_OP_DEADLINE_CEILING_MS (240 s) because the owned-labels capability is minted on one route with a 5-minute TTL and never re-minted; the loop stops on the teardown headroom rather than orphan a billable sandbox. Whether a four-minute service is worth advertising is SVC-008 §9.1 and is UNRULED.

E9-3-service-health-projection.reason: E9's exit gate names `health`, and this is the control-plane half of it: the projection that turns a durably-ingested service observation into `service_instances.status`. WHAT WAS TRUE BEFORE: SVC-008b emitted the five frozen service events and the JOB-005 ingest stored them, and they PROJECTED NO STATE CHANGE -- SVC-008b's own result says so in terms ("adds NO consumer of `recordServiceHealth` and no `service_health` projection ... every service event emitted here is durably stored and projects no state change"), and E9-1's reason records the consequence: SVC-002's reconciler converged zero instances to one and went quiescent, because nothing could drive an instance terminal. PRODUCTION CALLERS, measured with this guard's own `countProductionCallers`, base `6b39c77f6` vs head: `applyServiceProjectionForFence` 0 -> 1 (the per-event branch inside `acceptEvent`, itself on the shipped JOB-005 ingest path `workerControlRoutes` -> `createJobEventIngestService.ingest` -> `repos.jobControl.acceptEvent`); `writeServiceInstanceStatus` 0 -> 2 (the projection and `recordServiceHealth`, which now share the ONE writer of that column so the two cannot drift); `decideServiceProjectionForEvent` 0 -> 1; `predecessorsOf` 0 -> 1; and `canTransitionServiceInstanceStatus` 0 -> 1, which is the point of that last line: the FROZEN `SERVICE_INSTANCE_TRANSITIONS` table had ZERO production consumers at base, so the lifecycle it defines was a clause nothing enforced. `recordServiceHealth` is 2 at base and 2 at head -- unchanged, because the projection does not call it; both are entry points onto the shared writer. `createStartupReconciler`, the cautionary zero-caller neighbour, is untouched at 0. WHAT THE CLAUSE CLAIMS, NARROWLY: an accepted worker event that WITNESSES an instance fact moves `service_instances.status` inside the same fenced transaction that appends it, idempotently on a `service_instance_status` projection receipt, and every other event moves nothing. The authority for WHICH row is `service_instances.job_id`/`.attempt_id` (SVC-002's attribution), never the worker-controlled `payload.serviceInstanceId` -- which is unauthorized by construction (E9-F003), so a mismatched claim is REFUSED. The generation on the instance row is the FENCE SVC-002 scoped out by name, and a stale-generation event is refused. Legality is the frozen transition table, so no event can move an instance OUT of `stopped`/`failed`/`lost`: that is the DE-12 split-brain refusal, because a terminal instance has left `service_instances_live_service_uq` and SVC-002 has already replaced it. An attempt with no attributed instance answers `unattributed` -- an explicit unknown that writes nothing, never a default status. WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM, and each is the difference between this clause and E9's gate: (1) NOTHING CREATES A SERVICE -- `services` still has one insert with zero production callers and no route (SVC-007), so on a real deployment there is no instance for this projection to move; E9's exit gate is NOT met and this ticket does not claim it is. (2) The rest of SVC-003's Outcome is NOT delivered: no liveness deadline (a worker that goes silent without emitting anything is still only reaped at the LEASE level, and nothing terminalizes its instance), no graceful-stop or checkpoint request path, and no bounded lease-renewal change. SVC-003 stays OPEN. (3) Memory/context callbacks and connector refresh under the current fence are NOT built and are not buildable yet -- `MemoryActor` has no `service` kind and no memory op exists among the ten frozen worker operations (SVC-001-design.md section 4). (4) No partition test: no replica identity or partition detector exists anywhere in the tree. PROVEN, NOT DECLARED: server/src/__tests__/service-health-projection.integration.test.ts (11 cases over real embedded PostgreSQL and a real poll/ACK-minted ACTIVE fence, T1 driving the FULL `createJobEventIngestService` path so the decider is proven reachable from the wire -- and T1 is the ONLY case that drives that ingest, so the production wire is proven by exactly ONE arm: the `serviceProjection: null` mutant below reds T1 and nothing else, which is both the arming discrimination and the thinness) and server/src/__tests__/service-health-projection.test.ts (15 pure cases over the whole 9x9 transition table). SEVENTEEN mutants were applied to the shipped source, each VERIFIED APPLIED by a harness that tries both line-ending forms of its anchor and throws when it matches nothing, run, and reverted; every one killed at least one of the 26 cases while the NAMED positive control (`T8 POSITIVE CONTROL -- the batch attempt/job projection is byte-identical`) stayed green under all seventeen. The kills: delete the `attempt_started` -> `leased` arm (10 red -- without it `pending` is a dead end and the whole projection is production-unreachable), map `service_instance_started` to `healthy` (5), return the transition table unfiltered (7), project `stopping` from `service_graceful_stop_observed` (1), default an unreadable health verdict to `healthy` (2), REINSTATE `"interrupted"` in the health-status domain (2 -- this is the genuine BASE-TREE state, E9-F001), delete the legality check (1 -- T5, the split-brain case), trust `payload.serviceInstanceId` (1 -- T4), delete the generation fence (1 -- T3), return a definite `applied` for an unattributed observation (1 -- T7), have the projection bump `leases.expires_at` (1 -- T6, E9's "health events do not extend ownership" clause), delete the call site in `acceptEvent` (10 red, positive control still green), set `serviceProjection: null` in the ingest's `toAcceptInputs` (1 -- and ONLY T1, which is exactly the arming discrimination: the feature wired to nothing while every other case passes), and the four added by the review fixes -- revert `predecessorsOf` to the direct-edge filter (3), delete the attempt-terminal backstop (3), default `whenAlreadyTerminal` to `"noop"` (2, one of them T5 itself), and walk back through PROJECTABLE states too (3). ★★★ TWO REAL DEFECTS IN THIS DIFF WERE FOUND BY EXTERNAL REVIEW, NOT BY THE SUITE, AND BOTH WERE PERMANENT WEDGES -- recorded here because the shape of the miss is the point. (i) E9-F004: `SERVICE_INSTANCE_TRANSITIONS` makes `stopping` the SOLE predecessor of `stopped` and NO frozen worker event can assert `stopping` (the supervisor emits `service_instance_stopped` directly from `healthy` at `runServiceLifecycle`'s `case "process_exited"` arm at service-lifecycle.ts ~:293, and `gracefulStop`'s `verdict === "stopped"` branch at ~:362), so the first revision's direct-edge legality predicate refused EVERY NORMAL SERVICE STOP as `illegal_transition`, leaving the instance inside `service_instances_live_service_uq` where the reconciler could never replace it. It survived a named positive control and thirteen killed mutants because the only end-to-end case drove `service_instance_lost`, which the frozen table makes reachable from every non-terminal status -- a lifecycle table proven over the transitions a suite happens to exercise is not proven over the table. Fixed by admitting paths whose every INTERMEDIATE step is a status no event can project; the residual (`stopped` now admitted from `leased` too) is FILED as E9-F004 and stays open. (ii) E9-F005: a launch resolving no handle emits no `service_instance_started` (`runServiceLifecycle`'s §4.2a launch comment at service-lifecycle.ts ~:166 says so in terms), so a failed attempt left the instance `leased` forever; fixed with the attempt-terminal backstop and filed as E9-F005, resolved here.

E9-4-service-liveness-deadline.reason: E9's exit gate names `health` AND `restart`; SVC-003a wired the first half and this is the piece between them: the deadline that notices an instance is no longer live WHEN NOTHING SAID SO. WHAT WAS TRUE BEFORE: every path SVC-003a built is edge-triggered by an accepted worker event, and SVC-003a's own result says the gap in terms -- "a worker that goes silent WITHOUT EMITTING ANYTHING is still only reaped at the LEASE level, and nothing terminalizes its instance". Measured at head before this ticket: `reapExpiredLeases` revokes the lease and terminalizes the ATTEMPT and the JOB and contains no write to `service_instances` at all, so the instance stayed inside `service_instances_live_service_uq` and SVC-002's reconciler could never replace it. That is the case L-T8 measures rather than asserts. The dangerous variant is worse: `lease-renewal.ts` renews on a driver separate from the supervise loop, and `runServiceLifecycle`'s health step handles an unanswerable `processStatus` read with `unknown => EMIT NOTHING` (its own comment closes "SVC-003 owns the liveness DEADLINE policy"), so a worker whose supervision has gone silent while renewal continues holds a lease that never expires and is invisible to the reaper entirely. PRODUCTION CALLERS, measured with this guard's own `countProductionCallers`, base `053f90fc8` vs head: `sweepOrganizationServiceLiveness` 0 -> 1 (the pass inside `createServiceReconciler`'s own `runTick`, ahead of the convergence pages); `sweepServiceInstanceLiveness` 0 -> 3, of which only ONE is a call -- the guard also counts the repository interface declaration and its implementation, the same reason SVC-003a records 2 for `recordServiceHealth`; `classifyServiceInstanceLiveness` 0 -> 1; `livenessVerdictTerminalizes` 0 -> 1; `livenessDeadlineAllowedFromStatuses` 0 -> 2 (the sweep and the module's own load-time coverage assertion); `SERVICE_LIVENESS_DEADLINE_TO_STATUS` 0 -> 3; `writeServiceInstanceStatus` 2 -> 3 (the deadline is the THIRD entry point onto the one writer of that column, so it cannot drift into a fourth idea of a legal move); `predecessorsOf` 1 -> 2. UNCHANGED and re-measured rather than recited: `applyServiceProjectionForFence` 1 -> 1, `createServiceReconciler` 2 -> 2, `recordServiceHealth` 2 -> 2, `reapExpiredLeases` 3 -> 3, and the cautionary neighbour `createStartupReconciler` 0 -> 0. WHAT THE CLAUSE CLAIMS, NARROWLY: a live `service_instances` row whose worker has stopped being observed is driven to the frozen `lost` status by a clock rather than by an event, it leaves `service_instances_live_service_uq`, and SVC-002's unchanged reconciler creates its replacement -- in the SAME tick, because the sweep runs ahead of the convergence pages. TWO WINDOWS, AND THEY NEVER SUBSTITUTE: an instance that HAS been observed is aged against a short liveness window; one that has NEVER been observed has no liveness fact to age and is aged against `created_at` under a separate, longer admission window. Collapsing them in either direction is a defect with a name and both are mutation-pinned (L4/L15 for the short-window collapse, L5 for the infinitely-stale collapse). WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM, and each is the difference between this clause and the epic's gate: (1) NOTHING STILL CREATES A SERVICE -- `repos.services.insert` has the same ZERO production callers it had at base and this ticket adds no route (SVC-007), so on a real deployment the sweep reads an empty population and terminalizes nothing. (2) `service_generations` still has no writer, so a replacement stalls at `no_generation` on a real deployment exactly as SVC-002 records. (3) The deadline terminalizes the INSTANCE and does NOT fence the WORKER: it writes exactly one table (L-T11, mutant L17), so a silent-but-still-renewing worker keeps its lease while its replacement starts. The replacement is protected by SVC-003a's split-brain refusal; the old worker's external effects are not, and that residual is filed as E9-F006 and belongs to SVC-005's overlap clause. (4) WHETHER a terminalized instance should be replaced at all, and with what backoff, is SVC-004's crash-loop clause and this ticket has no opinion about it. PROVEN, NOT DECLARED: server/src/__tests__/service-liveness-deadline.test.ts (15 pure cases) and server/src/__tests__/service-liveness-deadline.integration.test.ts (11 cases, real embedded PostgreSQL, real poll/ACK-minted ACTIVE fence, the real shipped reaper). SEVENTEEN mutants were applied to the shipped source by a harness that refuses to apply over an existing backup, tries BOTH line-ending forms of every anchor and THROWS on a miss, rebuilds `dist` for repository mutants, and byte-verifies each restore; a green unmutated baseline was measured before and after the campaign. Every one killed at least one case and the NAMED POSITIVE CONTROL (`L-T9 POSITIVE CONTROL -- SVC-002's convergence is untouched by the deadline`) stayed green under sixteen of the seventeen. L7 is the exception and is a NON-RUN rather than a survival: it makes the module throw at load, so neither suite collects and no case executes, the control included -- said this way because a control that did not run is not a control that held. ★ ONE MUTANT SURVIVED THE FIRST CAMPAIGN AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN DROPPED: L14 (delete the sweep's independent legality gate) killed NOTHING, because `lost` is legal from all six live statuses so the gate is unreachable through the shipped caller. The gate was kept and pinned by a case that performs the narrow call itself (L-T10), the same shape SVC-002's T1c uses for its own unreachable property.

E0-de19-denial-audit.reason: DE-19's `audit` clause, "context retrieval and denials are recorded in the retrieval audit" — the first crossing closed out of the seventeen in the denial-audit class (E0-F010's eight + E0-F013's nine). ENROLLED IN THE SAME COMMIT AS THE SYMBOL, deliberately: `jobAuditBridge` is the cautionary tale — it was BUILT as this class's intended vehicle, has ZERO production callers to this day, and is not enrolled in this register at all, so nothing has ever reported on it (scripts/finding-ownership.json's separate MEDIUM finding). A writer nothing calls is the defect, not the fix. PRODUCTION CALLERS: ONE, and the number is stated as the guard measures it, not as it feels. The single textual call site is inside `handleMemoryGet`'s `denyMemoryGet` closure (server/src/mcp/tools/read-tools.ts), reached from THREE deny branches of the MCP `memory.get` tool (`not_visible`, `not_approved`, `actor_filter_denied`). An earlier draft of this sentence said "2 callers" by counting branches as call sites; `--counts` reports 1 and 1 is right. PROVEN, NOT DECLARED: server/src/__tests__/de-19-memory-denial-audit.integration.test.ts provokes the REAL cross-department refusal through the REAL handler against a REAL Postgres and asserts the durable row's WHO/TENANT/RESOURCE/WHY separately — it was observed RED before the change (3 failed / 4 passed) and four mutants were killed: deleting the write, stamping a constant reason, writing the row on the success path, and dropping the actor to "system". SCOPE, STATED NARROWLY: this wires ONE crossing. DE-19 itself stays `partial` because its authentication/revocation/integrity clauses are separately absent (E0-F016), and the other sixteen denial-audit crossings are untouched — four of them (DE-04/DE-12/DE-29 and DE-13's capacity half) additionally need a SEPARATE-TRANSACTION lifecycle this writer does not yet have, because their deny is a throw inside the tenant transaction that rolls back.

E3-5-product-approval.reason: JOB-010..014 parity bridge. Zero production callers; the legacy approval path still owns this. Wire when the sinks cut over (Sprint 6, MIG-005/006/007 ACTIVE).

E3-15-budget.reason: Parity bridge with ZERO production callers (jobBudgetCostBridge, server/src/services/job-budget-cost-bridge.ts:150; its entrypoint priceAcceptedUsage :231 is referenced only by server/src/__tests__/job-budget-cost-parity.integration.test.ts and server/src/__tests__/job-distributed-drain.integration.test.ts). MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: a handed-off distributed run is UNBILLED. WHERE AN OPERATOR ACTUALLY READS THIS -- NOT HERE. Until 2026-09-07 this sentence read 'READ IT BEFORE ARMING AOA_DISTRIBUTED_EXECUTION_ROLLOUT', which is an instruction to a reader who is not present: this file is a CI register, and the document an operator follows to arm the dial is docs/replatform/epics/E7-coding-e2b/tickets/CLI-006-staging-canary-runbook.md ('Audience: the OPERATOR'), section 2.1 'The rollout dial (canary mode)' and section 3 step 3, which carried no budget warning at all. W16A-FIX put the warning THERE and left the measurement HERE; this entry now points at the runbook instead of standing in for it. A warning shelved where the actor never looks is the shape this programme calls a check that nothing runs. Until 2026-09-07 this entry said 'budget/cost still flow through the legacy cost-event path'. That is FALSE, and it was the standing answer to the money question printed on every green policy run; E3-F037 refuted it and REMAINS OPEN, because what is corrected here is the sentence and not the gap. MEASURED at 8075cd7a1: the repository has exactly four insert(costEvents) sites -- server/src/services/company-portability.ts:3203 (bundle import), server/src/services/costs.ts:69 (costService.createEvent), server/src/services/heartbeat.ts:2653 (inside updateRuntimeState, declared :2622) and server/src/services/one-shot-cli-budget.ts:182 (recordOneShotCliCost, extraction) -- and none of them serves a handed-off run. heartbeat's writer has exactly two call sites, :5805 (success) and :6013 (inside the outer catch opened at :5960), and BOTH sit downstream of `return; // CLI-006-SUPPRESSION-RETURN` at heartbeat.ts:5451, inside `if (shouldSuppressLegacyExecution(canaryExecutionOwner))`. A return is not a throw, so a suppressed run reaches neither: no cost_events row, no increment to agents.spentMonthlyCents or companies.spentMonthlyCents, and checkBudgetAlerts (declared heartbeat.ts:2681, called at :2676 from inside that same function) never runs. Every control that could cap or pause reads that one ledger, so all three are blind to the spend: budget_policies through getObservedCents (server/src/services/budgets.ts:21 -- used by the warning/hard-stop evaluator at :238 and by the admission gate getInvocationBlock at :345, :368, :392, :414), the per-agent budgetMonthlyCents pause (checkBudgetAlerts sets agents.status='paused'), and the crew/company hard-stop (server/src/services/crew-budget.ts:121 preflightCrewDispatch, summing cost_events by company over the calendar month at :210-217). Until it does, the dial must not be armed for an Organization whose spend must be capped -- stated in the operator's own words at CLI-006-staging-canary-runbook.md section 2.1.
